note: The join policy (R+D.md §14.4, RD_14.4_HOSTILE_JOIN_PLAN.md). Named by $AT_JOIN_POLICY; absent is inert, and a file that does not validate stops the node at start. `anchors` chooses which out-of-band evidence makes an identity one this node trusts before the cohort it joins tells it anything: verified_contact (a first-contact contact whose safety number was compared, or a device its operator vouched for), zta (a credential chaining to one of our trust anchors and bound to the identity), operator (a node under THIS node's operator key: a verified operator-key binding, or a sibling device). unverified_contact is also accepted and deliberately left out here: a forwarded invitation link is enough to hold one. A class needs its extension (first_contact for contacts, zta for credentials, either for operator) or the node refuses to start. told_tier and own_evidence_min bound what the cohort's word alone can do: a peer this node holds no own evidence about reads at most told_tier until it has own_evidence_min entries of this node's own (its own halves of bilateral transactions, physics and calibration findings included), when the score built from that evidence alone takes over; probe verdicts count as own entries. An anchored peer is not bounded. burst_k, burst_interval_sec and burst_budget_factor shape the join burst: the bootstrap worker probes each bounded peer until it holds burst_k probe verdicts (default own_evidence_min), one probe per burst_interval_sec, spending at most burst_budget_factor x N x burst_k probes over N targets. anchored_cohort_min is how many of the cohort's members this node must count as anchors before it forms an anchored cohort with them: a second group beside the cohort, its own key and reputation chain, the lowest uuid among them minting it and inviting the rest.
